name: Invivyd, Inc.

profile.description: Invivyd (formerly Adagio Therapeutics) develops monoclonal antibodies to protect against serious viral infections, starting with COVID-19. Its commercial product, PEMGARDA (pemivibart), is authorized under an FDA Emergency Use Authorization for COVID-19 pre-exposure prophylaxis in moderately-to-severely immunocompromised people, and it generated $14.3M of net revenue in Q2 2026 (+21% YoY). Its lead pipeline asset, VYD2311, is in the DECLARATION trial for broader COVID-19 prevention. Chairman Marc Elia became CEO on September 1, 2026. The stock trades near $0.58, down more than 80% from its 52-week high of $3.07, with a market cap of about $172M.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): After its first antibody, adintrevimab, failed to reach market, the company rebranded as Invivyd and won Emergency Use Authorization for PEMGARDA, creating a new revenue stream that grew to $14.3M in Q2 2026 (+21% YoY) [1][2]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI-powered products or quantified AI-driven savings were found [4]. Market Share (2/2): PEMGARDA is the only monoclonal antibody authorized for COVID-19 pre-exposure prophylaxis in immunocompromised patients, which makes Invivyd the leader of that niche [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): VYD2311 is in the fully enrolled DECLARATION trial, with top-line data guided for mid-2026 [6]. The searches did not confirm the readout outcome, and the stock's roughly 80% decline from its 52-week high adds uncertainty [3]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D was $29.4M in Q2 2026, about 2x revenue, and 134% of TTM revenue, far above the commercial-biotech average [2][3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Invivyd's purpose of protecting vulnerable people from serious viral infectious diseases, beginning with COVID-19, is clear and patient-focused but not yet validated by years of consistent execution [1]. Community Impact (0/2): No foundation, charitable program, or quantified community investment was found [7]. Employee Retention (0/2): Glassdoor shows a 2.7 rating, 32% recommend-to-a-friend, and 50% CEO approval from a small sample. A May 2025 review describes no culture and no CEO during an extended interim period with the CFO as principal executive officer [4]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying was identified.

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Scored mechanically as a Growth stock. D/E is negligible at 4.6% (1.0), but TTM ROE is -59.7% (0, 2x) and TTM net margin is -184% (0) because operating expenses ballooned to $58.8M in Q2 2026 against $14.3M of revenue [2][3]. TTM revenue grew 26.3% to $58.4M (1.0) [3]. No 5-year revenue CAGR exists because commercial sales began in 2024, so that metric is excluded. Forward P/E is not meaningful and excluded, because consensus EPS stays negative through FY2028 (-$0.16). The provider's forward PEG of -0.04 is negative and scores 0 (2x) [3]. Weighted sum 2.0/7 gives a score of 3. The liquidity floor is passed at about $2.9M per day (5.08M shares x $0.58), though the sub-$1 price creates Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance risk.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Invivyd makes FDA-regulated biologic antibodies administered by infusion, and AI cannot substitute for that product or for the clinical and regulatory work behind it [1][6]. AI-accelerated antibody discovery at larger rivals could compress Invivyd's development advantage over time, but no analyst has flagged AI as a risk to the business [4]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-derived revenue exists.

infinite_game.summary: Invivyd has a service-oriented purpose of protecting immunocompromised patients that Sinek would respect in principle. In practice the company behaves like a binary clinical-stage biotech: CEO turnover, an extended interim leadership period, weak employee sentiment, and a strategy tied to the outcome of a single trial. It is playing to survive the next readout more than to advance a cause across decades.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): Protecting vulnerable people from viral disease is meaningful, but the company is only five years old, rebranded after its first product failed, and has not shown its purpose shaping decisions through a leadership transition [1][5].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management roughly tripled R&D to $29.4M per quarter to fund the DECLARATION trial of VYD2311, accepting a widened $44.4M quarterly loss to pursue broader COVID-19 prevention [2][6].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): A 2.7 Glassdoor rating with 50% CEO approval, reviews describing leadership speaking poorly of staff, and repeated executive changes, including an extended interim period with the CFO as principal executive officer before the chairman took the CEO role in September 2026, point to a low-trust environment [4][5].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Moving from Adagio's failed adintrevimab to the PEMGARDA and VYD2311 platform under the Invivyd name was a substantive reset, but it was driven more by necessity than by a long-term cause [1][5].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary framing vaccine makers or other antibody developers as rivals to learn from was found. Public messaging focuses on regulatory positioning [5].

investment_thesis: Invivyd owns the only authorized monoclonal antibody for COVID-19 pre-exposure prophylaxis in immunocompromised patients. PEMGARDA revenue grew 22% YoY in Q1 2026 and 21% in Q2 2026, to $14.3M [1][2]. With $160.1M of cash and negligible debt against a market cap of about $172M, the enterprise value is only about $20M, so the market assigns almost no value to VYD2311, which targets the much larger general COVID-19 prevention market if DECLARATION succeeds [2][3][6].
thesis_continued: The bear case is severe. The quarterly net loss widened to $44.4M in Q2 2026 from $14.7M, and at that pace cash covers only about three to four quarters, which makes dilution likely [2]. The stock has fallen from a 52-week high of $3.07 to about $0.58, which signals that the market doubts the VYD2311 opportunity, and the sub-$1 price risks Nasdaq listing-compliance issues [3]. PEMGARDA relies on an EUA and a narrow patient population, and leadership instability with weak employee sentiment adds execution risk [4][5].
key_catalysts: Disclosure and regulatory path for VYD2311 following the DECLARATION trial readout [6]
Continued double-digit PEMGARDA growth during the 2026-27 respiratory season [1]
Financing or partnership that extends the cash runway beyond 2027 without heavy dilution [2]
key_risks: Cash burn of about $45M per quarter against $160M of cash, which makes an equity raise at depressed prices likely [2]
Nasdaq minimum-bid deficiency with shares below $1, and potential reverse split or delisting [3]
Regulatory or policy changes to COVID-19 EUA products, and a narrow immunocompromised market limiting PEMGARDA's scale [1]
